subsystem.name: CrtRuntimeSupport
subsystem.responsibility: CRT-style runtime support layer: buffered stream I/O (read/flush/write/close/factory), OS-version-dispatched heap allocation/reallocation/size with pool fallbacks, critical-section management, TLS block access, fatal error/exit handling, time breakdown with timezone/DST, path resolution, and string/character/memory utility helpers.

summary: Twenty-five runtime-support functions reconstructed as CRT-style infrastructure. A BufferedStream type (fields +0x0 pointer, +0x4 count, +0x8 data start, +0xC flags, +0x10 OS handle) is served by StreamGetChar, BufferFlushWrite, FileStreamClose, StringWriteToFile, the lock/validate/unlock wrapper, and the FdopenWithMode factory, all bracketed by a common critical-section lock/unlock pair. A CrtHeapAllocator layer dispatches on an OS-version code (dword_8D4908) between region/large-pool (value 3), block-pool (value 2) and raw HeapAlloc/HeapReAlloc/HeapSize strategies, with an OOM-callback retry gated by a debug-heap flag (dword_8D41B0); ValidateAllHeapSlots sweeps the thread-heap slot array as an integrity check. CriticalSectionEnter/Leave are dispatcher helpers routing low indices to a lazy-init array and high indices to the imported Enter/LeaveCriticalSection. Fatal error/exit handling (CRTAmsgExit, ErrorHandlerWithOptionalCleanupThenExit) share the error-display flag dword_8D3EBC and cleanup call, terminating with 0xFF. TLS block access via +2/+3 DWORD getters feeds path resolution and file I/O error slots. TimeSecondsToBrokenDownTime applies timezone bias and DST handling above a 259200-second threshold. All proposals are DERIVED; ownership of every function is UNKNOWN at the packet level.

function_roles.role: Converts elapsed seconds or absolute timestamps to a broken-down time structure with timezone bias and DST adjustment; thresholds at 259200 seconds, DST marker at structure index 8.
Reads one buffered byte from a stream under the critical section, refilling via sub_58C255 on underflow; decrements remaining count at +0x4 and advances the pointer at +0x0.
Locks a stream buffer, validates it as a memory block via MemoryBlockValidationCheck, and unlocks; null argument short-circuits through sub_58A0BF.
Flushes buffered bytes to the OS file handle when write mode and initialization flags are set; resets buffer pointers, sets error flag on partial/failed write, returns -1 on failure.

Sweeps the thread-heap slot array (dword_8D4A24 / dword_8D5A40) and validates 0x83-flagged entries under per-slot and global critical sections; counts clean slots in mode 1, reports failed writable streams in mode 0.
CRT _amsg_exit-style error-exit handler: optionally displays the error dialog when dword_8D3EBC==1, runs cleanup via sub_5932F3, then calls the registered exit function off_5E65B0 with 0xFF.
Fatal error handler: displays message when dword_8D3EBC==1, runs cleanup via sub_5932F3, then terminates via ExitProcess with exit code 0xFF; __noreturn.
Generic forward iterator invoking a __thiscall callback a4(a1) exactly a3 times, advancing the element pointer by stride a2; returns the final counter.
nh_malloc entry: rejects sizes above 0xFFFFFFE0, attempts low-level allocation sub_58A973, retries after the GlobalCallbackDispatcherWithNullCheck OOM callback when the retry flag is set.

16-byte-aligned allocation wrapper dispatching on dword_8D4908: code 3 sub-allocates small blocks via sub_59416F under critical section 9, code 2 pulls blocks from the pool via sub_594C12, otherwise HeapAlloc; every pool path falls back to HeapAlloc.

Counted allocator (count * element size): rounds to a 16-byte boundary, dispatches through dword_8D4908 pool paths, zero-fills successful pool allocations via sub_58BB10, falls back to HeapAlloc(hHeap, 8u), and retries through the OOM callback when dword_8D41B0 is set.
Safe string formatting wrapper: sets a size counter, formats a2/a3 via sub_58D04D into the a1 buffer, then NUL-terminates or takes the sub_58CF35 failure path when the counter is exhausted.

CRT _fdopen-style stream factory: validates the open-file slot against uNumber, allocates a stream via sub_58C5AC, parses the mode string, ORs default flags dword_8D41BC, records the descriptor and increments the open-file count.
Returns the TLS block base advanced by 2 DWORDs (8 bytes), obtained via TLSValueRetrievalWithInit; used by file and path error-slot writers.
Returns the TLS block base advanced by 3 DWORDs (12 bytes), obtained via TLSValueRetrievalWithInit.

CRT fclose-style stream close: reads the file-handle index at +0x10, locks, flushes via BufferFlushWrite, clears stream flags at +0xC, resets the per-handle buffer descriptor, closes the OS handle via sub_58C724, releases the critical section.

memmove-style copy with overlap detection: backward copy when the destination lies inside the source range, otherwise DWORD-aligned forward bulk copy with jump-table-dispatched alignment and byte-tail completion; returns the destination address.
Character lowercase conversion: multibyte-encoding-aware path via sub_591FA1 when dword_8D3F38 is set, else ASCII fast path adding 32 to uppercase letters.

Reallocation wrapper dispatching on dword_8D4908: code 3 region-tracked realloc, code 2 pool-allocator realloc, otherwise raw HeapReAlloc; NULL input allocates, zero size frees, OOM callback retry when dword_8D41B0 is set.
Critical-section-guarded entry into path resolution: enters lazily-initialized section key 12, delegates the query to sub_58B92A, leaves the section, returns the query result.

Resolves a file path to its absolute form with a drive-letter prefix and ':.\' relative prefix via GetFullPathNameA, or the current directory via GetCurrentDirectoryA; writes TLS error codes 12/13/15/34 on failure paths.

Writes a length-prefixed string into a buffered stream under the critical section: measures via Strlen, locks, writes via sub_5886A7, conditionally clears stream fields, unlocks, returns 0 on full write else -1.

Queries the usable size of an allocation: dword_8D4908 code 3 reads the region header via sub_593E1B, code 2 scales the pool block index via MemoryRegionValidationHeapLookup, otherwise falls back to HeapSize; runs under critical section 9.
Critical-section enter dispatcher: index >= 20 calls the imported EnterCriticalSection at base+32, otherwise delegates to CriticalSectionLazyInitEnter(index + 28).
Critical-section leave dispatcher: index >= 20 calls the imported LeaveCriticalSection at base+32, otherwise delegates to CritSectLeave(index + 28).

classes.name: BufferedStream
classes.responsibility: CRT FILE-style buffered stream: byte reads with underflow refill, buffered flush to the OS handle, stream close, string writes, stream factory with mode parsing, and lock/validate/unlock wrappers, all protected by a shared critical-section protocol.

classes.name: CrtHeapAllocator
classes.responsibility: Heap allocation, reallocation, block-size query and heap-slot validation layer dispatching on an OS-version code (dword_8D4908) between region/large-pool, block-pool and raw HeapAlloc/HeapReAlloc/HeapSize strategies, with an out-of-memory callback retry gated by the debug-heap flag.

classes.name: CriticalSectionManager
classes.responsibility: Dispatcher helpers that route critical-section index below 20 through the lazy-init array and index 20+ to the imported Enter/LeaveCriticalSection at base+32.

classes.name: TimeConverter
classes.responsibility: Converts seconds or absolute timestamps into a broken-down time structure with timezone bias and daylight-saving adjustment, splitting at a 259200-second threshold.

classes.name: TlsBlockAccess
classes.responsibility: Provides per-thread data block base pointers advanced by fixed DWORD offsets for error-slot and file-state access.

classes.name: PathResolver
classes.responsibility: Resolves file paths to absolute form with drive-letter prefixing and current-directory fallback, reporting failures through TLS error slots; entered under a critical section.

classes.name: MemoryCopyRoutine
classes.responsibility: memmove-style copy with overlap detection, aligned bulk copying and jump-table-dispatched alignment and tail completion.

classes.name: CharacterCaseConverter
classes.responsibility: Converts a character to lowercase, using a multibyte-encoding conversion path when enabled or a plain ASCII fast path otherwise.

classes.name: SafeStringFormatter
classes.responsibility: Size-limited safe string formatting with NUL termination and a failure path when the format size counter is exhausted.

classes.name: CrtErrorHandler
classes.responsibility: CRT error/exit handling: optional error dialog, cleanup, and process or exit-function termination with code 0xFF.

classes.name: ForwardCallbackDriver
classes.responsibility: Generic forward iteration over a caller-supplied element array, invoking a __thiscall callback per element with a fixed stride.

interfaces.name: CriticalSectionAccess
interfaces.purpose: Uniform enter/leave over the runtime critical sections: stream-buffer lock (0x0058C1B1) and unlock (0x0058C203) plus the dispatcher helpers (0x0058C1E0 / 0x0058C232) that route low indices to the lazy-init array and high indices to the direct import path.

interfaces.name: BufferedStreamIo
interfaces.purpose: Observable buffered-stream operations: byte read (0x00589FCC), flush (0x0058A05A), close (0x0058AFE1), string write (0x0058BABB) and the external byte-write primitive (0x005886A7); callers must bracket access with CriticalSectionAccess.

interfaces.name: MemoryAllocationApi
interfaces.purpose: Observable allocation entry points a replacement runtime must provide: allocation wrapper (0x0058A935), nh_malloc (0x0058A947), aligned alloc (0x0058A973), free (0x0058AA6F), realloc (0x0058B5D4) and block-size query (0x0058BB68).

compatibility_contracts.name: NhMallocSizeGuard
compatibility_contracts.description: Allocation requests larger than 0xFFFFFFE0 return NULL without attempting an allocation (0x0058A947); a replacement allocator must preserve this guard.

compatibility_contracts.name: OsVersionPoolDispatch
compatibility_contracts.description: Allocation, reallocation and size queries dispatch on dword_8D4908: 3 uses region/large-pool paths (sub_59416F family), 2 uses the block-pool path (sub_594C12 family), anything else uses raw HeapAlloc/HeapReAlloc/HeapSize; callers that depend on block layout require the dispatch to be preserved.

compatibility_contracts.name: BufferedStreamLockProtocol
compatibility_contracts.description: Stream operations (byte read, flush, write, close) must bracket buffer access with the enter (0x0058C1B1) / leave (0x0058C203) critical-section pair so concurrent file I/O remains serialized.

compatibility_contracts.name: BufferedStreamLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: Stream struct offsets evidenced: +0x0 current pointer, +0x4 remaining count, +0x8 data start, +0xC flags, +0x10 OS handle. Field +0x4 has conflicting interpretations (remaining count vs buffer start) pending runtime evidence.

compatibility_contracts.name: FatalErrorExitContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Fatal error paths display a message when dword_8D3EBC==1, run cleanup via sub_5932F3, then terminate with exit code 0xFF through either the registered exit function off_5E65B0 or ExitProcess; termination must never return to the caller.

compatibility_contracts.name: TlsErrorSlotReporting
compatibility_contracts.description: Path resolution reports failures through per-thread TLS slots: validation failure writes codes 15 and 13, too-small caller buffer writes 34, allocation failure writes 12; callers read these via the TLSOffsetGetter family.

compatibility_contracts.name: TimeBreakdownThreshold
compatibility_contracts.description: Time conversion treats inputs above 259200 seconds as absolute timestamps (subtract timezone bias dword_5E7758, apply DST via dword_5E775C/dword_5E7760, flag index 8) and smaller values as time-of-day offsets normalized by mod 60/60/24.

compatibility_contracts.name: CriticalSectionIndexProtocol
compatibility_contracts.description: Critical-section index below 20 routes through the lazy-init array (slot at index+28); index >= 20 routes to the imported Enter/LeaveCriticalSection on the LPCRITICAL_SECTION at base+32.

unresolved: BufferedStream field +0x4 is read as a remaining-byte count by StreamGetChar (decrement, underflow refill) but as a buffer-start pointer reset by BufferFlushWrite; the packet offers no single interpretation and the conflict needs runtime evidence.
The broken-down time structure produced by sub_592787 (indices 0-8) is not covered by any packet field evidence ref; only the input field this+0x0 is evidenced.
dword_8D4908 values 2/3 (OS-version pool discriminator) and dword_8D41B0 (debug heap flag) semantics are DERIVED from the surrounding corpus fill, not packet-confirmed.
The contracts of the pool/region routines sub_59416F, sub_594C12, sub_593E1B, sub_593E46, sub_594624, sub_594F3E, sub_594B76 and sub_594BCD are opaque at this level.

SEH-related globals (ScriptFrameProcessor 0x0058895C and stru_5B8CB8 / 5B8CD0 / 5B8D00 / 5B8D18 / 5B8D30) and the TLS guard bytes 0xFF00000000001692 / 695 / 69B do not appear in the raw decompilations; they belong to surrounding SEH frames.

Jump-table target mappings inside MemoryCopyWithOverlapHandling (jpt_58B18C / jpt_58B165 / jpt_58B314 / jpt_58B2F2) are assembly-level and not recoverable from the C listing; the listed loc_/byte_ globals are jump-table data and case targets.
TLS error codes 12/13/15/34 and the +2/+3 DWORD TLS offsets have DERIVED meanings only.
The meaning of dword_8D3F38 (encoding-path handle) and the 0x100 argument passed to sub_591FA1 are not established.
The identity of the exit function pointer off_5E65B0 and the writers of dword_8D3EBC are not visible in this packet.
sub_589CB5 appears as a callee of CRTAmsgExit in the fact table but is not called anywhere in the raw source body.
The 2147224447 upper bound in TimeSecondsToBrokenDownTime has no documented purpose in the packet.
The critical-section array layout dword_8D4920 (36-byte entries, per-handle open bit at entry+4) and the heap-slot array (dword_8D4A24 / dword_8D5A40) are taken from the raw source only.

All class fields use the packet's evidence base 'this'; equal offsets across classes (this+0x0 in BufferedStream, TimeConverter and MemoryCopyRoutine) are NOT merged because the packet proves no common ownership (rule 8). Class membership and field names carry the separation.
